I'm a research scientist at the [ALERRT Center](https://alerrt.org) at Texas State University, where I study the health, mortality, training, and public perception of first responders. My doctorate is in criminal justice (University of Cincinnati), and I did a postdoc in social genomics and epigenetics in the [Harden Lab](https://www.kpharden.com/) at UT Austin before coming home to Texas.

Off the clock, I am:

- A husband and father of two little girls
- A native Texan (sixth generation, or thereabouts)
- A Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt with passable skills — *ba dum tss*
- An academic nomad: criminology, then genomics, then population health
- An evangelical R user
- The worst *Cards Against Humanity* player you are likely to meet

The blog, [Left-hand Thoughts](../3_posts/posts.qmd), is where the overzealous applications of R to everyday problems end up. Posts are rare. I'm working on it.
